prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's criticality-aware area repair uses a fixed shrink factor 3.0 on critical macros' effective area; c034 showed x2 penalty (0.05→0.10 in a different variant) helped, c035 showed over-tightening hurts. Modestly increasing the shrink factor from 3.0 to 4.5 (x1.5) on the already-validated c024 mechanism strengthens the "don't move critical macros" preference without the over-tightening seen in c026, improving TNS broadly across all three cases.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1002:legalization overlap; bp_fe-ng45/1003:HBT min-spacing violation; bp-ng45/1001:KeyError in partition; bp-ng45/1002:KeyError in partition; bp-ng45/1003:KeyError in partition
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: mixed legality (overlap, min-spacing), crash (KeyError in partition), and timeout failures. Systematic across all seeds of both cases (bp_fe-ng45 and bp-ng45), so this candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. The KeyError in partition suggests the shrink-factor change broke a downstream partition lookup (likely missing/renamed critical-macro entries), cascading into legality and timeout. To make the idea legal: guard the partition lookup against absent critical macros, validate shrink factor bounds before repair, and re-run with per-stage timeouts to isolate the crash from the timeout.
